content.title: About
content.content: Beer with a higher alcohol content (typically 7 %–12 % ABV) is brewed with a larger amount of malt and sometimes additional ingredients such as spices or fruit extracts. It delivers a richer body, stronger bitterness, and a longer finish compared with standard light beers.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: High‑alcohol beers are often called “strong”, “imperial” or “barley‑wine” depending on the style.
Historically, these brews were used as a “nutritional” beverage for sailors and travelers.
Traditional styles like Belgian Quadruple and German Dunkel can exceed 10 % ABV.
Achieving high alcohol levels often involves double fermentation or adding sugar late in the process.
In many countries, strong beer is taxed at a higher rate than regular beer.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Dark malts and caramelized sugars used in the recipe are rich in polyphenols, which may help reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Fermentation produces B1, B2, B6 and folate, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Beer provides potassium, magnesium and phosphorus, essential for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Moderate consumption and cardiovascular effect
items.content: Some studies link moderate intake of strong beer with higher levels of “good” HDL cholesterol.

items.title: High alcohol content
items.content: The large amount of alcohol can lead to rapid intoxication, increased injury risk, and liver problems with regular use.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Strong beer contains over 200 kcal per 12 oz (≈330 ml), which may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Interaction with medications
items.content: Alcohol can amplify the effects of sedatives and reduce the efficacy of certain drugs.

items.title: Yeast allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to the yeast used during fermentation.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: Strong beer is usually served in 300–500 ml glasses at 10–13 °C to showcase its aromatic notes. It pairs well with aged cheeses, roasted meats, dark chocolate, and caramel‑rich desserts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the beer in a cool, dark place at 8–12 °C. Avoid direct sunlight and sudden temperature changes to prevent oxidation and flavor loss.
